Theme

treatment noun

medical

also medical treatment, therapy, cure, treat (a patient), be treated

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.4.1: plānē cūrātiōnēs ejus nōn probō
M-O s.v. therapy, treatment (medical)
Traupman 66, 397, 393
Traupman 65

cūrātiō, cūrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

medical treatment, cure

With the genitive of the illness (Traupman 66). To treat a patient or an illness: cūrāre (Traupman 66, 397); Lewis & Short call the medical sense very frequent.

Other words

  • cūra, cūrae f. — care, treatment

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cels. 2.10 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 166

  • medicīna, medicīnae f. — a remedy, treatment

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ov. Rem. 91: sērō medicīna parātur

    Also the art of medicine (see medicine).

  • therapīa, therapīae f. — therapy

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. therapy, treatment (medical) (1843); Traupman 393

Examples

  • sed plānē cūrātiōnēs ejus nōn probō

    but I really do not approve of his treatmentCic. Fam. 16.4.1

  • prīncipiīs obstā; sērō medicīna parātur, cum mala per longās convaluēre morās

    resist at the start: treatment comes too late when the trouble has grown strong through long delayOv. Rem. 91–92

  • cūrātiō therapeutica

    therapy treatmentTraupman 393

See also doctor, medicine, remedy, hospital, disease, operation, treatment.
